prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. These are actual screenshots of the current Yorimichi skate park. Redesign this specific park into a beautiful FLOWING seaside skate landscape. Produce one clear high aerial oblique architectural game concept at the same 112x88m pier scale and keep the surrounding blue sea and autumn forest game aesthetic. Diagnose visually by improving the obvious problems: currently a vast empty grey slab with isolated harsh rectangular ramps, giant raised bathtub bowl, jagged tan surface artefacts, dead vertical backs, tiny thin rails, little coherent composition. Transform the riding surfaces into connected landforms: a unified western terraced street plaza with long run-up decks, four/seven stairs, proper handrails and hubbas, banks wrapping the terraces into the flat; a central low smooth wave/hip joining lines; sweeping low perimeter return banks to keep motion circling; the eastern bowl integrated into sculpted surrounding banks instead of sheer bunker walls, connected to a southern mini-ramp through curved berms. Retain usable flatbar and manual-pad lines with long uncluttered roll-outs. Add graceful pale sand/terracotta paving bands defining the flow of the lanes and rounded landscaped islands OUTSIDE skating lines, with coastal grasses, low curved seatwalls, warm timber shade structures. Warm ivory concrete, sage riding surfaces used sparingly, terracotta edge bands, copper-red rails, rich dark timber, contrasting bronze perimeter fencing. Believable skateable geometry with tangent joins, smooth up-and-back transitions and no abrupt edges across approaches. Give the space identity through design and landform, not clutter. No annotations, arrows, labels, people, UI or photorealism. Make something far better composed than these screenshots, while achievable as clean low-poly meshes.
